incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Law (Ley de Sociedades de Capital); Articles 20-22 (public deed and incorporation), 23-28 (articles of association), 58-59 (registered office), 124-127 (sole administrator), 213 (first appointment of officers). Law 14/2013 on Support for Entrepreneurs is available for expedited electronic incorporation where eligible.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name certification; the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the province of the registered office for the final incorporation filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), which must be submitted for registration in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum paid-up share capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash; the payment must be evidenced by a bank blocked-deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution. The blocked amount is released only upon execution of the public deed. Higher capital may be agreed in the articles of association.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: FIRST, the share capital of EUR 3,000 (three thousand euros) is fully subscribed and paid in cash, evidenced by the bank blocked-deposit certificate attached to the incorporation deed. SECOND, the registered office of the company is established at [Calle Ejemplo 123, 28001 Madrid], Spain, and the Administrator shall notify the Commercial Registry and tax authority of any subsequent relocation. THIRD, the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Sole Administrator, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Data Protection Officer. FOURTH, the Sole Administrator is expressly authorized to execute the public deed, obtain the definitive tax identification number (NIF), file the company with the Commercial Registry, and register the company with the Social Security and municipal authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Corporate Name Certificate from the Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Calle Príncipe de Vergara 94, Madrid; online through the RMC website (www.rmc.es)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a negative name certificate requesting reservation of the proposed corporate name. Provide at least two alternative names. The certificate is valid for three months. Reserve the name in the exact legal form applicable to a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada by indicating the suffix 'SL'.
required_dossiers: Official name reservation application form
List of proposed corporate names in order of preference
Copy of the promoters' identity documents or passports
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
Proof of payment of the official certification fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity to an existing registered name, promptly submit amended applications with new alternative names. If the certificate expires before incorporation, reapply for a fresh certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital in a Blocked Bank Account and Obtain Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution or bank branch legally operating in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company being incorporated and deposit at least EUR 3,000 in cash. The bank will issue a blocked-deposit certificate specifying that the funds are held for the incorporation and may not be withdrawn except by the notary upon deed execution.
required_dossiers: Corporate name certificate issued by the Central Commercial Registry
Identity documents of the shareholders or legal representatives
Bank's internal account-opening forms
Declaration of source of funds for compliance with anti-money-laundering rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate due to identity or source-of-funds issues, correct the documentation or select another Spanish financial institution. Ensure the deposit references the exact proposed corporate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Incorporation Deed before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary Public (Notario) of the jurisdiction where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders or their authorised representatives must appear before the notary to execute the incorporation deed. The notary will review the draft articles of association, shareholder identity details, capital deposit certificate, and name certificate. The deed must include the firm name, business purpose, registered office, capitalisation, administration structure, and first officers.
required_dossiers: Valid corporate name certificate
Bank blocked-deposit certificate
Draft articles of association (estatutos sociales)
Shareholders' passports or national identity documents
Foreign shareholders' Foreigner Identification Numbers (NIE) or proof of appointment
Original signed shareholder resolution appointing the first officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a substantive criticism or requires amendments, amend the draft articles and reschedule execution. After execution, a first copy (primera copia) of the deed is delivered for registration; correct any typographical errors by a notarial corrective instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Provisional NIF and File Censal Form 036 with the Tax Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT) – Central or territorial office depending on the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before or immediately after deed execution, file Form 036 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to obtain the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional). This NIF is required to complete subsequent registrations before the Commercial Registry and Social Security.
required_dossiers: Public incorporation deed (or copy if submitted before deed execution)
Form 036 duly completed
Identity documents of the legal representative
Proof of the registered office address
Corporate name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected due to missing data, correct Form 036 and resubmit. If the provisional NIF is not received within the expected time, request issuance in person at the appropriate AEAT window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mercantile Registry of the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first copy of the public deed, together with evidence of payment of stamp duties and the provisional NIF, to the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry. The registry examiner will verify the legality of the deed and issue a registration certificate. The company acquires legal personality only upon registration.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public incorporation deed
Provisional NIF certificate or issuance receipt
Proof of payment of notarial and registry fees
Completed application for registration
Identity document of the notary or authorized attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'nota de calificación' listing defects, cure each defect within the statutory period and submit corrected documentation or apply for a new notarial deed. If registration is delayed, file a written appeal to the Directorate General for Legal Certainty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Final NIF, Register with Social Security, and Complete Municipal and Sectoral Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; General Treasury of Social Security (TGSS); Local Municipality (Ayuntamiento); Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Commercial Registry registration, present the registration certificate to AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF. Register the company and its administrators with TGSS for employer social-security obligations. File Form 036 with the new registered-data status, pay the municipal economic-activity tax, and obtain the municipal activity license if the company will maintain a physical office. For the digital platform, submit prior communication to the Spanish Data Protection Agency and comply with Law 34/2002 on information-society services.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry registration certificate
Definitive NIF application form or updated Form 036
Public deed and corporate bylaws
Director and employee identification documents
Municipal activity license application and premises documentation
Privacy policy and cookie policy for the digital platform
Data processing register and Data Protection Officer appointment, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF conversion is delayed, provide the registry certificate to AEAT in person. If the municipal license is queried, submit architectural floor plans or obtain a technical report. For AEPD, correct the processing activity register and resubmit the communication.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Council (Ayuntamiento) of the registered office for the economic-activity and opening license; Secretariat of State for Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence (SEDIA) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for digital-services regulatory coordination.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Prior Communication for Information-Society Services (Comunicación Previa de Actividad) under Law 12/2012 and Law 34/2002 LSSI, together with the Optional Fast-Track Activity License (Licencia de Apertura) if a physical office is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge (MITECO) and, where relevant, the competent regional environmental agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the business operates as a digital editorial platform with no physical industrial installation, no production plant, and no significant environmental footprint; only a municipal activity communication is required for professional office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for wastewater or VOC emissions because the platform operates through cloud infrastructure. If the company controls physical servers, comply with the EU Code of Conduct for Data Centre Energy Efficiency and Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE). For any controlled office waste, follow municipal segregation and disposal ordinances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate and building occupancy inspection are required only if the company obtains a municipal opening license for a physical office; the premises must comply with the local fire-protection installation regulations and the Technical Building Code. A workplace risk assessment and emergency plan must be prepared under Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention. No civil-defense clearance is mandated for a purely digital serialised web-novel platform operating from a software and editorial workspace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) at https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by submitting AEAT application with passport copy, company incorporation documents, and registered office proof. Processing requires 30-60 days. NIF functions as statutory TIN; VAT number is NIF prefixed with country code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive; limited regime elections exist for digital platform operators under Spanish VAT and corporate tax codes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Facturación Electrónica Real-time reporting via SII (Sistema de Información Inmediata) with API integration for immediate VAT clearance and digital fiscal stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported outside EU territory and services supplied to non-EU recipients. Eligibility requires documented proof of export such as goods leaving Spanish customs territory or services performed for non-resident clients.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating triggers fines up to 100% of VAT amount, interest surcharges, retrospective refund clawback, and potential criminal tax evasion proceedings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under full current account convertibility pursuant to EU acquis and IMF Article VIII obligations. Capital account transactions are liberalized with limited restrictions; prior notification or approval required for direct investments exceeding EUR 5 million or real estate acquisitions above national thresholds. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted subject to corporate tax compliance, beneficial ownership verification, and anti-money laundering due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies to digital service revenues. Export receipts must be reported to the Bank of Spain within 30 calendar days of collection via foreign trade statistics forms; conversion occurs at prevailing market rates with full FX transaction reporting required for statistical and tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible via licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorized by Banco de España such as PayPal Europe or local providers; legal constraints include minimum capital reserves of EUR 350,000, strict reserve fund obligations, and comprehensive AML/KYC obligations under Royal Decree 308/2022 for cross-border issuance and redemption.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video identification permitted for Spanish SL entities under current Banco de España guidelines; physical appearance of directors is not mandatory for standard onboarding but may be required for accounts exceeding EUR 100,000 or complex beneficial ownership structures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via Spanish IBAN accounts using SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'; verification requires matching beneficiary details, source of funds documentation, tax authority clearance for non-resident investors, and beneficial ownership disclosure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails via SWIFT MT103 for trade settlements; Commercial Letters of Credit available through correspondent banks for international trade; all disbursements require prior FX approval if exceeding thresholds and proper tax withholding at source under Spanish tax regulations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SLs (first €300,000 of positive taxable base in the first two tax periods); R&D&I credits 25-42%; capitalization reserve 10% reduction; participation exemption 100% on qualifying dividends/capital gains (holding ≥5%, 1 year); Startup Law 15% for emerging entities (additional).
